dedupe_keys.name: arlunz agent based rural land use model new zealand

description: ARLUNZ (Agent-based Rural Land Use New Zealand) simulates the land-use decisions of individual farmer agents across a catchment, choosing between dairy, sheep and beef, forestry and other uses with heterogeneous behaviour, social networks and economic optimisation, to explore how climate policy changes rural landscapes. It was developed by Fraser Morgan and Adam Daigneault of Landcare Research and published in PLOS ONE in 2015. It is applied to New Zealand catchments and coupled, through Python 2.7, with the New Zealand Forest and Agriculture Regional Model (NZFARM), which supplies farm economics. The model runs in NetLogo 5.0.5 with GIS, String and Shell extensions; the article is open access under CC BY 4.0 and states that the data are in the paper and its supporting information. Caveats: it is tied to old NetLogo and Python versions and to NZFARM inputs, so reuse needs porting. The study found farm revenue grew despite greenhouse gas pricing, emissions fell through forestry on marginal land, and a $60 per tonne carbon price cut net emissions by about 54% against the baseline. For simulation it shows how agent-based farm models can test climate adaptation and mitigation policies and the land-use change that drives demand for rural water, roads and energy. It is related to the MPMAS and Mediterranean land-use wildfire model records in this catalogue, other farm agent-based models.
